receiver.message_back:
Dear Counsel,

Thank you for sending the Seller’s initial draft. We have reviewed the draft and have the following principal comments on behalf of the Buyer.

First, based on the Buyer’s preliminary review of the business and the limited protections currently reflected in the draft, the proposed USD 45,000,000 purchase price is not acceptable. The Buyer is prepared to proceed on the basis of a purchase price of USD 38,000,000, subject to confirmatory diligence and agreement on customary protections.

Second, the proposed 30-day closing period is too compressed. We propose that closing occur within 60 days after signing, subject to satisfaction of customary conditions precedent and completion of the Buyer’s confirmatory diligence.

Third, the representations section should be expanded materially. At a minimum, the Seller should provide customary representations regarding title to the shares, accuracy and completeness of financial statements and disclosed information, absence of undisclosed liabilities, taxes, compliance with laws, litigation, material contracts, no material adverse change, and authority/enforceability.

Fourth, the agreement should include customary indemnification for breaches of representations and covenants and for pre-closing tax matters, supported by an appropriate escrow or holdback.

Finally, the confidentiality covenant is acceptable in concept, provided it includes customary exceptions for disclosures to affiliates, advisers, financing sources, and as required by law or regulation.

Please let us know whether the Seller is prepared to proceed on this basis, and we would be pleased to turn a revised draft promptly.

Best regards,
Bellweather Croft LLP

Dear Counsel,

Seller is not prepared to move to USD 38,000,000, but in the interest of advancing the transaction has revised the purchase price to USD 42,000,000. We have also proposed a 45-day outside closing period, subject to customary conditions, while avoiding an open-ended diligence condition.

Best regards,
Aldous Finch LLP

edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 42,000,000 for the Shares at Closing, by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated by the Seller.

2. Closing. Closing shall occur as promptly as practicable, and in any event within 45 days after signing, subject to satisfaction or waiver of the conditions precedent set forth in this Agreement, including receipt of any required third-party consents and the continued accuracy in all material respects of the representations and warranties as of Closing. Buyer’s confirmatory diligence shall be completed during such period and shall not constitute a separate condition to Closing except to the extent expressly set forth in this Agreement.

3. Representations. The Seller represents and warrants to the Buyer that: (a) the Seller has good and valid title to the Shares, free and clear of all liens other than restrictions arising under applicable securities laws; (b) the Seller has authority to enter into and perform this Agreement, and this Agreement constitutes a valid and binding obligation of the Seller, enforceable in accordance with its terms; (c) the financial statements and other written information provided by the Seller to the Buyer are, to the Seller’s knowledge, accurate and complete in all material respects and fairly present the financial condition and results of operations of the Company for the periods presented; (d) except as disclosed to the Buyer, to the Seller’s knowledge, the Company has no material undisclosed liabilities; (e) except as disclosed to the Buyer, the Company is in material compliance with applicable laws; (f) except as disclosed to the Buyer, all material taxes required to be paid by the Company for pre-Closing periods have been paid or adequately reserved; (g) except as disclosed to the Buyer, there is no material litigation pending or, to the Seller’s knowledge, threatened against the Company; (h) the material contracts disclosed to the Buyer are in full force and effect in all material respects, and, to the Seller’s knowledge, neither the Company nor any counterparty is in material breach thereof; and (i) since the date of the most recent financial statements provided to the Buyer, there has not occurred any material adverse change in the business, assets, liabilities, financial condition or results of operations of the Company, except for changes affecting the industry or general economic conditions generally and not disproportionately affecting the Company.

4. Confidentiality. The terms of this Agreement and all non-public information concerning the Company and the transaction are confidential and shall not be disclosed by either party, except to such party’s affiliates, directors, officers, employees, advisers, accountants, attorneys, financing sources and representatives who have a need to know and are informed of the confidential nature of such information, or as required by applicable law, regulation, legal process or stock exchange rule; provided that, to the extent legally permissible, the disclosing party shall give the other party prompt notice of any legally required disclosure and reasonably cooperate to limit the scope of such disclosure.

5. Indemnification. From and after Closing, the Seller shall indemnify and hold harmless the Buyer and its affiliates from and against losses arising out of (a) any breach of the Seller’s representations and warranties, (b) any breach of the Seller’s covenants, and (c) pre-Closing taxes of the Company, in each case subject to the limitations set forth in this Section. No claim for breach of representations and warranties may be made unless and until aggregate losses exceed USD 250,000, after which only the excess shall be recoverable. The Seller’s aggregate liability for breaches of representations and warranties shall not exceed 10% of the Purchase Price, except in the case of fraud, willful misconduct or breaches of the representations regarding title to the Shares or authority. At Closing, USD 2,100,000 of the Purchase Price shall be deposited into escrow for 12 months to secure the Seller’s indemnification obligations, pursuant to an escrow agreement reasonably acceptable to the parties. Claims for breaches of representations and warranties must be made within 12 months after Closing, except for claims relating to title, authority, fraud, willful misconduct or taxes, which shall survive for the applicable statute of limitations.

receiver.message_back:
Dear Counsel,

Thank you for the revised draft and cover note. Buyer appreciates Seller’s movement and the addition of a more complete indemnity framework.

We have reviewed the draft, including the mark-up. As a drafting point, the proposed indemnification provision appears to remain in tracked changes rather than being integrated into the visible operative text. Please incorporate it as a standalone Section 5 in the clean draft.

Commercially, Buyer is prepared to move from its prior position, but USD 42,000,000 is still above where Buyer can proceed given the remaining diligence, consent and recourse issues. Buyer can sign promptly at USD 40,000,000, subject to the following revisions:

1. Purchase Price: USD 40,000,000.

2. Closing / Diligence: 45-day outside closing date is acceptable, provided Buyer has a closing condition for no material adverse issue identified through confirmatory diligence and satisfactory receipt/review of required consents and material contracts.

3. Representations: The expanded categories are helpful, but the knowledge and disclosure qualifiers are too broad. Financial statements, undisclosed liabilities, compliance with law, taxes, material contracts and no material adverse change should be brought down without general knowledge qualifiers, subject to specific disclosure schedules.

4. Indemnity: Section 5 should be included in the operative text, with: basket reduced to USD 150,000; escrow increased to 7.5% of purchase price; escrow period extended to 18 months; general cap increased to 20% of purchase price; and title, authority, taxes, fraud and willful misconduct excluded from the basket and cap. Pre-closing taxes should be recoverable dollar-for-dollar.

5. Confidentiality: The proposed exceptions are acceptable in concept, provided recipients are informed of and bound by confidentiality obligations at least as protective as the agreement.

If Seller can agree to the above, Buyer is ready to turn a clean draft promptly and move to signing.
